_readme: Reversals this tree declares, for scripts/ci/check-silent-revert.py (ADR-1284).
A reversal is only silent when nothing in the repository says it was meant.
An entry is not a path exclusion: the gate matches a finding against it only
when the detector, the exact path, the commit being undone and every single
evidence line all agree, so the entry covers one migration and stays silent
about anything else that later touches the same file.
Fields: adr (the decision that supersedes the reverted work), kind (which
detector), undoes (full target sha, mandatory for reverse-hunk), paths
(exact repository paths), evidence (a regex every matched line must satisfy),
reason (what a reviewer needs in order to agree).
A one-off revert with no ADR behind it is declared in the PR instead:

reversals.reason: c2a3c7e0f (#1067) rewrote every dataset path from `.corpus/` to the retired numbered workspace directory. ADR-1277 (Accepted, 2026-09-20) names that rename `the incorrect first migration attempt` and splits local data into `.workingdir/` for machine-local state and `.corpus/` for datasets; scripts/ci/check-local-data-contract.sh is the required gate that keeps the retired root out. Restoring `.corpus/` in these files is that decision landing, not work being lost. The evidence regex is written `\.workingdir\d?` rather than naming the retired root, because scripts/ci/check-local-data-contract.sh forbids an active file from spelling it; it still holds the entry to the path text: across all sixteen files every line this finding rests on carries the retired root or `.corpus/`, and nothing else of c2a3c7e0f is touched.

The `buf_dev` tier is ADR-0759, landed by 31a51afb2 (#101) and silently reverted by 92ea978a4 (#102) — the pair ADR-1284 was written from. Master still carries the reverted state, so restoring it is text master once held and lost coming back, which is what `resurrected` is for. docs/state.md records it as T-HIP-ADM-BUFFER-BY-POINTER-REVERTED-2026-09-21 and docs/rebase-notes.md tells the next rebase how to resolve it. The branch's own 6811ef63d writes these lines; the finding survives only because the later unwind-helper reconciliation re-indents a second copy of each, so the merge holds one more occurrence than any single commit added.

HISS-01: init()'s `goto fail` unwind moved into adm_state_release(), which close() now calls too, so each early return frees exactly what it allocated. The five lines are the old cascade -- three `goto fail;`, the three `if (!s->...)` guards that fed them and the shared `return -ENOMEM;` -- and every one of them is live in the rewrite, at a different indent or inside the helper. Nothing of master's is lost: master and the branch's own parent carry byte-identical blobs for this file (git rev-parse 6c8e7b8ea:core/src/feature/float_adm.c == 5b4aec35a:...), and the edit was authored inside the merge commit d9805a64f itself, which is why no non-merge branch commit's diff contains the removal and `dropped` fires. ADR-0141 is the rule that obliges the cleanup: every file the merge touched goes to zero HISS findings. Scores were re-measured on all three Netflix golden pairs at --precision max, byte-identical apart from the fps field.

reversals.reason: HISS-01: the first-append branch of vmaf_model_collection_append() and its three cascading unwind labels (fail, fail_mc, fail_model) moved into model_collection_new(), which frees locally on each early return in the same order -- mc->model before mc. All 29 lines are that block; every allocation, memset, strncpy and comment of it stands in the helper, re-indented by one level, and the caller still leaves *model_collection NULL on failure. Master and the branch's own parent hold byte-identical blobs for this file, so the merge lost nothing of the target's: the edit was authored inside merge commit d9805a64f, which is why branch intent does not contain it. ADR-0141 obliges it.

reversals.reason: One HISS-01 and two HISS-04 clearances in one file. extract()'s forward `goto write_score` became an `if (!s->motion_force_zero)` wrapper around the SAD block; init()'s ISA dispatch chain moved into motion_select_pipeline() with the guards and their order intact; flush()'s per-index loop body moved into motion_flush_one() with the loop-carried prev_processed threaded through a pointer. All 50 lines are those three bodies, re-indented -- no statement was rewritten and no arithmetic changed, so every emitted score is bit-identical. Master and the branch's own parent hold byte-identical blobs for this file; the edit was authored inside merge commit d9805a64f, so no non-merge branch commit's diff carries the removal. ADR-0141 obliges it.

The mirror image of the `dropped` finding on the same file and the same edit. Pulling flush()'s loop body into motion_flush_one() shifts it one indent level left, so `} else {` and the motion_blend continuation `s->motion_max_val);` reappear at column widths this file carried before an earlier commit indented them. The text is not target work coming back; it is the same two lines the refactor re-indented, which is why they are also absent from every non-merge branch commit's diff. ADR-0141 obliges the split.

The ADM_CM_LINE(rows_per_thread) generator macro had exactly one expansion, ADM_CM_LINE(8), and the HISS-04 scanner read `ADM_CM_LINE(8);` at file scope as a signature whose body ran to the next `{` -- reporting the anonymous namespace below as one 127-line function. The macro is written out token-for-token as adm_cm_line_kernel_8, which also matches how the HIP twin spells it. The sixth line, `const int32_t add_bef_shift_flt = (int32_t)(1u << (shift_flt - 1));` and its ADR-0155 comment, is the same value written as INT32_MIN so NVCC 13.4's diagnostic #68-D goes away; the emitted bits are unchanged (docs/research/2076-cuda-adm-signbit-warning.md). Master has not touched this file since the merge base 7e20ab78d (git rev-parse 7e20ab78d:<path> == 6c8e7b8ea:<path>), so the merge removed nothing of the target's.

HISS-04: i4_adm_cm_device_hip()'s region arithmetic moved whole into i4_adm_cm_region_hip(), returning an I4AdmCmRegionHip. Every statement moved unchanged and in the same order, so the launch geometry is identical; the 16 lines are the four clamp expressions and the twelve `&name` argument slots that are now spelled `&r.name`. Master has not touched this file since the merge base 7e20ab78d, so nothing of the target's is lost. The file also carries a second, separate declaration in this allowlist (ADR-0759, kind `resurrected`); the two cover different lines and neither covers the other.

reversals.evidence: (TIDY_RATCHET_PREP_|nvcc, hipcc and icpx compile through meson custom targets|translation units out of compile_commands\.json; add them before measuring)
reversals.reason: ADR-1290 renamed the per-lane compilation-database hook from TIDY_RATCHET_PREP_<lane> to TIDY_RATCHET_COMPDB_<lane> and gave every lane an entry, cpu and arm64 included, so a lane that needs no generator says so explicitly instead of expanding to nothing by accident. The six lines are the old hook: its two comment lines and the three cuda/hip/sycl assignments, plus the `$(TIDY_RATCHET_PREP_$(LANE))` expansion in both recipes. Both generators survive verbatim -- gen-gpu-compile-commands.py for cuda and hip, gen-sycl-compile-commands.py for sycl -- under the new names at Makefile lines 226-233, and scripts/ci/tests/test_tidy_ratchet_sycl_compdb.py pins that the hook runs. The rename landed in the branch's own cf2ad500b, but against a base whose recipes were laid out differently from master's, so branch intent does not line up with the merge effect.

reversals.evidence: (They become PR-required contexts as soon as a hosted|meson compiles `\.cu`|custom targets, which leave them out of|gen-gpu-compile-commands\.py` \(CUDA and HIP|gen-sycl-compile-commands\.py` \(SYCL\) against the|Without that step the lane measures the host files only)
reversals.reason: The same ADR-1290 rename in its operator documentation. The old single paragraph on the cuda/sycl/hip lanes was replaced by an expanded one that states every fact it stated and adds the two preconditions ADR-1290 records (-Db_lto=false and an out-of-repo build directory). The six lines read as gone only because the replacement re-wraps them: `Without that step the lane measures the host files only.` is now `Without it those lanes measure the host files only.`, `They become PR-required contexts as soon as a hosted` is now `These lanes become PR-required contexts as soon as a hosted`, and both generator scripts are still named, at docs/development/ci.md under `TIDY_RATCHET_COMPDB_<lane>`. Master has not touched this file since the merge base 7e20ab78d, so the merge removed nothing the target had added.

A single line of the changed-files tidy lane's exclusion list, and a pure merge-resolution artefact. The branch's 7c4cd4258 added the .config/hiss/testdata/ and compat/python-vmaf/matlab/ families, which ADR-1142 puts under the lane's scope rule: a family with no compile command is excluded here and bounded by its ratchet lane. On that commit's base the eBPF line was the last one and carried no trailing pipe; master had meanwhile appended `| python3 scripts/ci/pelorus_mirror.py filter` to it. The resolution keeps both: the eBPF exclusion is still there, now ending in a continuation backslash, the two new families follow it, and the pelorus_mirror filter still consumes the list. Nothing the target had is gone -- only the line's continuation character moved.

reversals.evidence: (HIP integer ADM kernels read their buffer description|pointer again \(ADR-0759\)\.\*\* The change listed|passed by pointer\" had been undone by a later merge|still copying the 328-byte struct|is back: each launch now passes one device pointer|byte-identical and 1080p throughput is unchanged)
reversals.reason: Two changelog fragments were written independently for one change -- ADR-0759's buf_dev tier being re-landed after 92ea978a4 undid it -- and they collided on the same filename. Master's six lines came in with #1507 at the merge base; the branch's 6811ef63d created the file from a base that did not have it (git cat-file -e 6811ef63d^:<path> fails). The merge keeps the branch's, which names the four kernels, both commits, and the measured ROCm 7.2 numbers on gfx1036/gfx1100/gfx90a, and so says everything master's said and more. The released changelog therefore still carries the entry; only the duplicate prose is gone.

reversals.reason: d170ef86a (#1531) replaced the shared ADR-0680 and ADR-0681 CLI helpers and bootstrap pattern in these three scripts with hand-written argparse and sys.path boilerplate. Restoring make_argument_parser, collect_cli_argv, and bootstrap_ai_script in PR 1553 implements accepted ADR-0680 and ADR-0681 per ADR-1291. Across all three files, every line this finding rests on carries either the old hand-written CLI/bootstrap shape from d170ef86 or the restored ADR-0680/0681 shared helper pattern, and nothing else of d170ef86 is touched.

reversals.evidence: ^\s*vmaf_log\(VMAF_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, "(?:Error: )?(?:device_id %d is out of range|failed to initialize CUDA)\\n"(?:, device_id)?\);$
reversals.reason: ADR-0848 (and BUG-048) standardizes stderr diagnostic records across the codebase to not duplicate severity prefixes already provided by vmaf_log(VMAF_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, ...). 5d070b0b4 (#515) had added 'Error: ' prefixes to device_id and CUDA initialization failure logs; removing them restores the standardized call-site format documented in docs/usage/cli.md and docs/rebase-notes.md, and verified by core/test/test_vmaf_log_callsite_format.py.

Restores ADR-0982 CUDA runtime partial-initialization and release error unwinding (BUG-048 Sec A3). a12373faa (#504) accidentally reverted fbde2f91e (#503) by routing vmaf_cuda_release failures to fail_after_pop, leaking the dlopen'd CudaFunctions driver table. Routing through fail_release_funcs and clearing cu_state restores the leak fix. Verified by core/test/test_cuda_runtime_unwind.c.

reversals.evidence: ^\s*vmaf_log\(VMAF_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, "(?:SpEED: image too small, operating width or height is 0|invalid speed_kernelscale)(?:\\n)?"\);$
reversals.reason: ADR-0848 standardizes diagnostic records into complete newline-terminated stderr lines. 5d070b0b4 (#515) omitted trailing newlines on the SpEED image-dimension and kernelscale error logs; adding '\n' ensures logs do not concatenate with subsequent stderr output. Documented in docs/usage/cli.md and docs/rebase-notes.md, and verified by core/test/test_vmaf_log_callsite_format.py.

Restores ADR-0982 SYCL graph extractor registration ordering (BUG-048 Sec A3). a12373faa (#504) accidentally reverted fbde2f91e (#503) by moving combined_queue allocation after num_graph_extractors++, leaving state corrupted if queue creation failed. Allocating the combined queue before incrementing the extractor count restores safety against null-dereference crashes on submit.

Research-2096 and PR #1556 resolve CodeQL Alert 1230 (cpp/unused-static-function) in default LTO builds by placing vector_unchanged under the FEX_VECTOR_ALLOC_TEST configuration guard that matches its callers, superseding 11a47f39b's [[maybe_unused]] attribute. As recorded in docs/rebase-notes.md, configuration-only helpers stay configuration-owned.

ADR-0726 removed the Vulkan backend from VMAFx. 5d070b0b4 accidentally reintroduced comments claiming Vulkan ran through GPU device plugins. Commit 4b9c040a5 removes the stale Vulkan wording from the Helm chart templates and guides, preserving active backends (CUDA, HIP, SYCL, CPU) as recorded in deploy/helm/vmafx/AGENTS.md and docs/rebase-notes.md.

ADR-0988 mandates routing strict RFC-8259 JSON serialization through vmaftune.jsonio.dumps_strict across all vmaf-tune emitter modules to prevent non-finite float tokens (NaN, Inf) from breaking parsers. fedce9889 had introduced a bare json.dumps in ladder.py; restoring dumps_strict fulfills ADR-0988 and is verified by test_emit_json_replaces_all_nonfinite_quality_values.
